standard_prerequisites.name: Chern classes of a perfect object and the capping operation of a bivariant class
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Section labelled section-pre-derived (source line 9042), used throughout the proof, and Situation labelled situation-setup (source line 1372) in the statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the objects P_p(E_2), c_p(E_2) and the bivariant Chow groups in which the characterised class lives.

core_obligations: Use the exact sequence for a cover by two closed subschemes to decompose an arbitrary alpha' in CH_k(X') as i'_{1,*}alpha'_1 + i'_{2,*}alpha'_2, with alpha'_2 well defined up to an element of the image of pushforward from X'_1 cap X'_2 (proof lines 9732-9739).
Define P'_p(E_2) cap alpha' = P_p(E_2) cap alpha'_2 and prove well definedness by the hypothesis that E_2 restricts to zero on X_1 cap X_2 (proof lines 9739-9742).

Treat the rank case: if E_2|_{X_1 cap X_2} is a finite locally free module of rank less than p in degree 0 then its p-th Chern class vanishes by rank considerations, so the identical argument applies to c'_p(E_2) (proof lines 9744-9748).
proof_roadmap: Decompose classes along the two-component cover and record the ambiguity of the second summand (proof lines 9732-9739).
Define the class and use the vanishing hypothesis to make it well defined (proof lines 9739-9742).
Repeat in the small rank case through the vanishing of c_p (proof lines 9744-9748).
difficulty_reason: For two closed immersions i_1, i_2 covering X set theoretically, a perfect object E_2 on X_2 whose Chern classes are defined and whose restriction to X_1 cap X_2 is either zero or a finite locally free module of rank less than p in cohomological degree 0, the lemma produces a canonical bivariant class P'_p(E_2), respectively c'_p(E_2), in A^p(X_2 -> X) characterised by two capping properties: on i_{2,*}alpha_2 it returns P_p(E_2) cap alpha_2, respectively c_p(E_2) cap alpha_2, and on i_{1,*}alpha_1 it returns zero, with the same after any base change (statement lines 9694-9724). The proof writes an arbitrary class alpha' in CH_k(X') as i'_{1,*}alpha'_1 + i'_{2,*}alpha'_2 using the exact sequence for a cover by two closed subschemes, notes that alpha'_2 is well defined only up to an element in the image of the pushforward from X'_1 cap X'_2, and shows that setting P'_p(E_2) cap alpha' = P_p(E_2) cap alpha'_2 is independent of that ambiguity precisely because E_2 restricts to zero on the intersection (proof lines 9730-9742). In the rank case the same argument runs because c_p of the restriction vanishes by rank considerations (proof lines 9744-9748). Seeing that the only obstruction to well definedness is the ambiguity coming from the intersection, and that the two hypotheses are exactly what kills it, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
